paras: The posse shooting of Bob Jones took place at about midnight on August 11, 1905, in Monroe, Louisiana, when a posse shot and dangerously wounded Jones, a Black brakeman on the Iron Mountain Railroad. Jones was accused of assaulting a conductor of the railroad, and his chances of recovery were reported to be small.

According to a dispatch from Monroe dated August 12, Jones was accused of having assaulted Conductor Haddon of the Iron Mountain Railroad on the preceding Wednesday, August 9. The dispatch does not describe the alleged assault or say what led to it. A posse had been searching for him from the time of the assault.

The posse located Jones in a house near the Planters' Oil Mill in Monroe. At about 12 o'clock that night he was shot while trying to escape from the house and was "dangerously wounded." The report added, without naming a source, that "it is said he fired on the posse as he ran from the house"; this account came from the side of his pursuers.

The dispatch called his chances of recovery small, but no later report of his death, recovery, arrest or trial appears in the coverage. The dispatch names neither the members of the posse nor any officer leading it.

The shooting is known from a single wire paragraph printed on page 5 of the Pensacola Journal on August 13, 1905, under the headline "Negro Shot By Posse." The item stated the assault on the conductor as fact rather than as a charge and passed on the claim that Jones had fired on the posse without attributing it. No coverage in the Black press, in Monroe papers or in other wire reprints was found.
